ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the circuit in the attached figure, the left side is a current source Is, with the current upward; a resistor R1 is connected in series above. After passing through R1, it reaches the upper node, which is simultaneously connected to the upper ends of the vertical resistor R2 and the right-side vertical resistor R3; the lower ends of R2 and R3 are connected at the same lower node, so R2 and R3 are in parallel. The voltage U is marked across R3, with polarity positive at the top and negative at the bottom. Reasoning: The current source provides Is = 1 mA, and after passing through R1 it enters the parallel node of R2 and R3. Since R2 = R3 = 1 kΩ, the resistances of the two parallel branches are equal, so the current is evenly divided: IR3 = 1 mA / 2 = 0.5 mA. The required U is the voltage across R3, therefore U = IR3 × R3 = 0.5 mA × 1 kΩ = 0.5 V.
